html:
The Wiradjuri are the largest Aboriginal Australian nation of New South Wales by area. Their country covers the central west of the state, the land of three rivers: the Wambool (Macquarie), the Kalare (Lachlan) and the Murrumbidjeri (Murrumbidgee).

They are united by kinship and shared law. Their neighbours included the Gamilaraay to the north, the Gundungurra and Ngunnawal to the east and the Yorta Yorta to the south.

The British crossed the Blue Mountains in 1813, and Bathurst was founded on Wiradjuri land in 1815. As settlers poured in, Wiradjuri resistance grew under Windradyne, and in 1824 the governor declared martial law around Bathurst, a conflict known as the Bathurst War.

In 1851 gold was found at Ophir near Bathurst, which set off the first Australian gold rush. Wiradjuri people survived on missions, stations and town edges, and the nation and its language are strong again today.
